{{Quote|Are you going to pay for that?''&raquo;<br/>"''Huh? Wanga?''"<br/>&laquo;''It costs seven wupiupi.|Gragra and Jar Jar Binks|<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>|translated=1}}
'''Gragra''' was a [[Swokes Swokes/Legends|Swokes Swokes]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] who lived on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], working as a [[Gorgmonger/Legends|gorgmonger]] in the [[City/Legends|city]] [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]]. She was regarded as the city's best gorgmonger, even though she grew her product within Mos Espa's sewer system. She would raise her [[Gorg/Legends|gorgs]] in a bucket of slime and prepared them for sale once they reached maturity. Gragra lied about where she procured her goods, claiming she grew them in a basement culture pool.

In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], travelling with the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], tried to steal a gorg from her Mos Espa stall. Gragra demanded seven [[Wupiupi/Legends|wupiupi]] from Binks, but soon considered the matter closed when the [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|podracer]] [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]] began to accost him.

==Biography==
===Gragra the gorgmonger===
[[File:Gragra the Gorgmonger.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Gragra was a Swokes Swokes gorgmonger living in Mos Espa.]]
The [[Swokes Swokes/Legends|Swokes Swokes]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] Gragra was a [[Gorgmonger/Legends|gorgmonger]] who operated<ref name="db" /> and lived<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Tatooine Limited|cardname=Gragra}}</ref> in [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]],<ref name="db" /> a port [[City/Legends|city]]<ref name="SWCTP">''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]''</ref> on her [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]],<ref name="db" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="TPM" /> She spent many [[Standard year/Legends|years]] selling her goods in the market area of the city,<ref name="FF89" /> and she had long become a fixture in the city's marketplace<ref name="SWCTP" /> by [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|I}} to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].</ref> Her shaded<ref name="SWCTP" /> street-corner<ref name="CCG" /> stall, right next to the [[Akim's Munch/Legends|Akim's Munch]] street [[Cafe/Legends|cafe]],<ref name="SWCTP" /> held a prime spot opposite one of Mos Espa's most popular cantinas.<ref name="FF89" /> She originally procured her [[Gorg/Legends|gorgs]] through the sewer system below Mos Espa.<ref name="FF99" /> 

Considered to be Mos Espa's best gorgmonger, she charged a premium of seven [[Wupiupi/Legends|wupiupi]] for her gorgs<ref name="FF89">{{FactFile|89|GOR 1-2|Gragra the Gorgmonger}}</ref> grown<ref name="db" /> alongside other edible [[Amphibian/Legends|amphibians]]<ref name="gorg db">{{DB|creature|gorg|gorg}}</ref> in a sewer zone in the city.<ref name="db" /> Her gorg-growing process started with placing a gorg pod in a bucket of slime and encouraging to hatch by getting the slime at the right [[Temperature/Legends|temperature]] and viscosity and maintaining its nutrient level. In about two [[Standard month/Legends|months]], the gorg tadpole would mature, and Gragra would feed them her own [[Diet/Legends|dietary]] supplements to improve their flesh's flavor and texure. Upon their maturity, the Swokes Swokes prepared them for sale.<ref name="FF99" />

Despite the truth, Gragra claimed she grew them in a large basement<ref name="db" /> climate-controled<ref name="FF99">{{FactFile|99|GOR 3-4|Gragra the Gorgmonger}}</ref> culture pool.<ref name="db" /> To combat the stench of the sewers, she hung her gorgs, tied at the legs, at her stall before selling them, reducing the sewer smell and hiding their origin. However, most of her customers knew where they came from, but did not care as the gorgs tasted good. The young<ref name="FF99" /> [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]]<ref name="Novelization" /> boy [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] frequently ate [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] from her stall.<ref name="FF99" />

===Gungan theft===
{{Quote|When the shopkeeper bounded out of the shop, demanding payment, Jar Jar opened his mouth and the frog snapped away. The tension of the wire sent the frog zinging into a bowl of soup, splashing the creature eating it.|Padmé Amidala, in her journal|<ref name="Journal">''[[Star Wars Journal: Queen Amidala]]''</ref>}}
[[File:JarJarGragra-TPM.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Jar Jar Binks stole from Gragra (right) at her stall.]]
During the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]]'s [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion]] of the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]<ref name="Novelization" /> in 32 [['ABY-BBY' dating system/Legends|BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> Gragra was operating her stall in Mos Espa. As she did, the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], who was disguised as a [[Handmaiden/Legends|handmaiden]], and the clumsy [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], were seeking out [[Starship/Legends|ship]] parts for the Queen's [[J-type 327 Nubian royal starship/Legends|starship]] in the city. As Amidala and Jinn walked past the stall, Binks,<ref name="TPM" /> who had not eaten in some time<ref name="Novelization" /> and thought the gorgs at Gragra's stall looked moist and tender, could not resist the gorgs<ref name="FF99" /> and snapped one up with his [[Tongue/Legends|tongue]]. Unfortunately for him, the gorg was tied to one of the stall's wires, stopping him.<ref name="Novelization" />

Gragra soon caught sight of the Gungan's attempted theft and asked him if he was going to pay for the gorg.<ref name="TPM" /> After she rushed out of her stall<ref name="Novelization" /> demanded<ref name="FF99" /> seven wupiupi from Binks,<ref name="FF99" /> the Gungan let go the gorg, but the<ref name="TPM" /> freshly [[Death/Legends|killed]]<ref name="Adventure">''[[Episode I Adventures 14: Podrace to Freedom]]''</ref> creature had been catapulted from the wire into<ref name="TPM" /> the [[Soup/Legends|soup]]<ref name="Novelization" /> of the [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|podracer]] [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]]. The Dug leapt from his table at Akim's Munch and accosted the Gungan,<ref name="TPM" /> allowing Gragra consider the matter between her and Binks closed.<ref name="SWCTP" /> As the Swokes Swokes watched, Skywalker stepped in and stopped the fight.<ref name="TPM" /> Amidala later documented the interaction between Gragra and Binks in her personal [[Padmé Amidala's journal|journal]].<ref name="Journal" />

She eventually left Mos Espa to work elsewhere, which caused the [[Gorg/Legends|gorg]] population in the sewers to grow considerably over the following years. Homeless people often fed on these gorgs.<ref name="SWG">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=terminal||Evict the Gorg Eaters}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
[[File:Gragra-FFp70.png|thumb|right|250px|Gragra had questionable hygine.]]
Gragra lived a hard life as a Swokes Swokes alone on Tatooine. The gorgmonger was wise enough to not get into street brawls with unpaying customers, even if she was considered imposing looking.<ref name="FF99" /> She did, however, get outraged when Binks attempted to steal a gorg from her.<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=1999 Topps Star Wars: Episode I Widevision Series 1|cardname=29 - Snagged by Sebulba|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/73014/cid/5263439/1999-Topps-Widevision-Star-Wars:-Episode-I-29-Snagged-by-Sebulba|archivedate=20260713070034}}</ref> Gragra did not mind growing gorgs and felt the slime was a welcome relief from Tatooine's heat.<ref name="FF99" /> A woman<ref name="db" /> of questionable hygine,<ref name="Saga">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Saga Collection|pack=#052: Gragra|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/tsc052gragra.asp}}</ref> she had<ref name="db" /> tough<ref name="FF89" /> [[Color/Legends|white]] skin, black<ref name="db" /> [[Horn/Legends|horns]],<ref name="FF89" /> and black colored [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="db" /> She held an affiliation to the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="FF89" />

==Skills and abilities==
The Swokes Swokes's claim of growing her gorgs in climate-controlled tanks demonstrated impressive business acumen.<ref name="FF99" />

==Equipment==
During her interaction with Binks, Gragra wore a brown [[Clothing/Legends|smock]], a black cummerbund, a dark brown skirt<ref name="SWCTP" /> over brown pants,<ref name="Saga" /> and a dark brown apron. She also wore brown bands around her [[Limb/Legends|arms]].<ref name="SWCTP" /> At her stall, she kept a collection of dried and succulent gorgs for hungry customers,<ref name="SWCTP" /> securely tied to wires,<ref name="Novelization">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref> and [[Gorg dipping sauce|gorg dipping sauces]].<ref name="VD">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The woman wielded a silver cleaver<ref name="Saga" /> and used a spatula.<ref name="Comic" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Appearances and adaptations===
{{Quote|Hey, that will be seven truguts!|An altered line from Gragra in Episode I's novelization|<ref name="Novelization" />}}
Gragra appeared in the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], in which the Akim's Munch scenes with the character were shot on [[July 29]], [[1997]], in [[Wikipedia:Tunisia|Tunisia]]. Gragra was revealed in the web documentary "It's Like War Now,"<ref name="It'sLikeWarNow">{{SW|url=video/it-s-like-war-now|series=Making Episode I Webdocs|text=Part 9: It's Like War Now}}</ref> released on [[March 15]], [[1999]].<ref name="Lynne Hale">{{SWArchive|url=episode-i/video/archive_lynnesdiary.html|text=Lynne's Diary Video Archive|archivedate=20020202192946}}</ref> The character later first appeared in the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]] of the film, written by [[Terry Brooks]]<ref name="Novelization" /> and published on [[April 21]], 1999.<ref name="YearByYear">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> Gragra was first identified on [[May 12]], 1999,<ref name="Calendar">{{Decipher|url=calendars/product/index.html|text=The Decipher Calendar}}</ref> with a card released in the ''[[Menace of Darth Maul]]'' expansion to [[Decipher]]'s [[Young Jedi Collectible Card Game|Young Jedi Collectable Card Game]].<ref name="YJCCG">{{YJCCG|set=Menace of Darth Maul|cardname=Gragra: Chuba Peddler|link=http://www.decipher.com/youngjedi/cardlists/menaceofdarthmaul/dark/images/86gragrachubapeddler.gif}}</ref>

Episode I, where Gragra was voiced by [[Toby Longworth]],<ref name="Longworth">{{WebCite|url=https://starwarsinterviews.com/prequel-trilogy/episode-i-the-phantom-menace/toby-longworth-lott-dod|text=Toby Longworth (Lott Dod)|author=[[Dennis Pellegrom]]|date=2017-06|work=[[Star Wars Interviews]]|archivedate=20230205201422|nolive=1}}</ref> later released on [[May 19]] of that year.<ref name="YearByYear" /> Longworth tried out several voices for the character to video playback at a recording studio, near [[Wikipedia:Abbey Road, London|Abbey Road, London]], while<ref name="Longworth" /> ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator<ref name="YearByYear" /> [[George Lucas]] directed him.<ref name="Longworth" />

The young readers book [[Jar Jar's Mistake|''Jar Jar's Mistake'']], written by [[Nancy Krulik]]<ref name="JarJar">''[[Jar Jar's Mistake]]''</ref> and published in [[April]] 1999,<ref name="Amazon">{{RandomHouseOld|url=kids/catalog/display.pperl?isbn=037580000X|text=Jar Jar's Mistake}}</ref> contains Gragra's confrontation of Binks, but removes any reference to a specific currency and has the character run off at Binks.<ref name="JarJar" /> Various adaptations of Episode I, including the novelization;<ref name="Novelization" /> the [[Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace 2|second issue]] of the film's [[Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace (comic series)|comic adaptation]], written by [[Henry Gilroy]]<ref name="Comic">[[Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace 2|''Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace'' 2]]</ref> and published on May 12, 1999;<ref name="DarkHorse">{{DarkHorse|url=Comics/98-044/Star-Wars-Episode-I---The-Phantom-Menace-2-of-4|text=Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace 2}}</ref> the [[Star Wars Manga: The Phantom Menace 1|first volume]] of the [[Star Wars Manga: The Phantom Menace|manga adaptation]]<ref name="Manga">[[Star Wars Manga: The Phantom Menace 1|''Star Wars Manga: The Phantom Menace'' 1]]</ref> released on [[December 22]], 1999;<ref name="MangaDate">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54222/star_wars_episode_i_-_the_phantom_menace_manga_1999_1|text=Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace Manga (1999) #1}}</ref> and the [[Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace (script facsimile)|script facsimile]]<ref name="Script">[[Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace (script facsimile)|''Star Wars'' Episode I: ''The Phantom Menace'' script facsimile]]</ref> released in [[February|Feburary]] [[2000]];<ref name="Collector8>{{CollectorCite|8|Around the Galaxy}}</ref> combine Gragra's two lines in the film and changes the wupiupi she asks for into [[Trugut/Legends|truguts]].<ref name="Novelization" /><ref name="Manga" /><ref name="Script" /> The [[Episode I Adventures 14: Podrace to Freedom|fourteenth installment]] to the ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Adventures]]'' series, written by [[A. L. Singer|A.L. Singer]] and published in [[October]] 2000, has the combined line but maintains the reference to wupiupi.<ref name="Adventures14">''[[Episode I Adventures 14: Podrace to Freedom]]''</ref>

===''Adventure Book'' appearance===
{{Quote|All these aliens are coming to eat. Help them get the correct food. When you're ready to start, click on the serving bell to let everyone know that we're open.|Gragra, to the player of ''Star Wars: Jar Jar's Journey Adventure Book''|<ref name="JJBook" />}}
Gragra appears in ''[[Star Wars: Jar Jar's Journey Adventure Book]]''&mdash;a [[Star Wars video games|video game]]<ref name="JJBook">''[[Star Wars: Jar Jar's Journey Adventure Book]]''</ref> released on [[November 12]], 1999<ref name="CB">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/videogames/news/news19991115.html|text=''Jar Jar's Journey'' Released}}</ref>&mdash;on its ninth page, which rougly follows the events with Gragra in the film. The player can click on four of Gragra's gorgs, a [[Clam/Legends|clam]], or a [[Bird/Legends|bird]], all of which Binks will try to consume. After the Gungan eats a gorg, Gragra will replace it. If the player clicks on the Swokes Swokes, she will shout a sales pitch.<ref name="JJBook" />

In the page's minigame, Gragra appears in the game's interface and walks through the player as they sell various types of food to [[Alien/Legends|aliens]]. Once the player opens, Gragra will shout out another sales pitch. When the player must select a food for an alien, going off the customer's description, the Swokes Swokes will ask the player what they think the alien wants.<ref name="JJBook" />
